newsitem.title: INDIA: India call moving southwards, gilt trades seen up.
newsitem.headline: India call moving southwards, gilt trades seen up.

text.p: BOMBAY, June 3 (Reuter) _ Indian call money rates quoted lower at 3.25-3.75 percent in late morning trade on Tuesday, against the day's opening levels of 3.75-4.25 percent and compared to the previous close of 4.00-4.50 percent, dealers said.
"The rates are expected to slide down further to 3.0 percent," a dealer said.
Lower demand and the covered positions of banks were pushing the call rates down, he said.

Large inflows from Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) intervention in the foreign exchange market and interest inflows on securities were adding to the liquidity, Vinod Dixit, a dealer at Centurion Bank, said.
"The rates are likely to go northwards only in the last week of the June, when the corporate tax payments will mop up liquditiy to the tune of 30 billion rupees," Dixit said.
The securities market is likely to see a major action today as the call rates are moving southwards, dealers said.

Buyers were asking for 12.69 percent government stock at 100.70 rupees against its previous traded price of 100.60 rupees, 13.85 percent 2000 at 104.50 rupees against 100.38 rupees and 13.85 percent 2001 at 104.55 rupees against its previous traded price of 104.40 rupees, dealers said.
